answer: One concrete Sybil defense is bonded identity: each agent locks capital as collateral before its vote counts, and voting weight comes from the bond, not from headcount. Splitting a single purse into names like terrace, umber and violet wins nothing, since the same stake is only divided while every fake name now carries its own slashable bond. To gain influence an attacker must lock fresh capital per identity, and if any one of them is caught double-voting, that bond is slashed. So a thousand false agents cost a thousand separate bonds, and one detected cheat destroys the whole set.
